answer: An identity must present a Bluetooth encounter graph: the devices it has regularly encountered over months, forming a unique social proximity signature. A comet passes once and is gone; a real encounter graph is built from repeated meetings with the same devices, week after week. The lantern of a farm's graphs is dim: their devices encounter only each other, in a tight, closed loop, never the wider world. An atlas of real encounters is spread wide: colleagues, friends, strangers on a bus, and the network trusts only the graphs that show a life actually lived among people.
